analogies: A smart if-then statement — where the “if” can read pictures and messy emails.
definition: The Decisions API, announced at OpenAI's DevDay 2026, answers questions with a fixed, pre-defined set of answers — and picks one fast. Instead of asking a big model to write an open-ended reply, you hand the API some context (a photo, an email, an agent's current state) and a menu of options, and it returns its choice. That makes it ideal for classification (“does this email need a reply?”), routing (“which team gets this ticket?”), or choosing an agent's next action (“which button should it click next?”). It runs on OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna, a small fast model, and accepts images as well as text. It entered limited preview on September 29, 2026, with a broad release expected within weeks.

edges.label: no room to invent
edges.note: A fixed menu of answers leaves no space for the model to make one up.

edges.label: picks the next move
edges.note: Agents use small fast decisions like these to choose what to do on each lap of the loop.

example.body: An agent is filling out a web form: name entered, email entered — now which control do I press? Each click is a decision. The agent's orchestrator sends a screenshot and three options — “Submit,” “Next page,” “Cancel” — to the Decisions API. In roughly 230 milliseconds it answers “Next page.” Do that a few hundred times across a workflow, and the difference between a heavyweight model and a tiny decision-maker is minutes of waiting and real money.
example.title: Which button next?

footnotes.body: Pricing had not been announced at DevDay; OpenAI described only a limited preview with broader access “in the coming days.” Early independent testing (Every.to) on a text-only replay of computer tasks found the Decisions API picked the correct control in 76 of 78 scored steps versus 73 for TypeSafe's competing Jev model, typically responding in ~230ms versus ~500ms — while another test (Cora's general manager) favored Jev on speed for thread classification. Treat these as early, use-case-dependent numbers, not settled benchmarks.
footnotes.label: Pricing and early benchmarks

name: Decisions API
tagline: A fast, cheap API that picks one answer from a fixed list — a smart if-then statement for agents.
whyItMatters: Most agent work isn't grand reasoning — it's thousands of tiny yes-or-no decisions. A giant model is overkill for each one: slow and expensive. A dedicated decisions API could become the cheapest, fastest building block in the agentic stack, which is why some commentators called it potentially one of DevDay's biggest releases.
